annotations.title: Set the words that make a file sensitive

description: The SCAN TERMS: words, phrases or symbols that make a file sensitive in nodata_scan_folder and nodata_plan, each with a label and a tier (1 public · 2 internal · 3 confidential · 4 restricted). The organisation's terms come from NoData when this computer is connected (cached here); the user's own are kept on this computer. A file holding a term is reported with the term's label, tier and count (never the text around it) and is raised to that tier in the plan. action 'search' answers "would the scan catch X?": how a column named X is judged, whether X is in the built-in list, in the user's or the organisation's terms, and (with path) how many files in a folder hold it, counts only; when nothing covers it, it gives the add call. Use it when the user names something sensitive the scan did not report. action 'amounts' with on:true treats money amounts as sensitive (the scan reports them, a clean copy replaces them with [AMOUNT]); off by default, because a clean copy is for working with the numbers. Turning it on asks for confirm:true; turning it off needs the user's own approval. Use it when the amounts ARE the secret (holdings, a family office). action 'list' shows both lists. 'add' adds one of the user's terms (asks for confirm:true). 'remove' removes one of the user's terms by id (needs the user's own approval). The organisation's terms are changed only at NoData.

approval.description: remove: the code the user approved.

confirm.description: add: true = do it. Omit to preview.

id.description: add: a short id (letters, digits, - _); default from the label. remove: the term's id.

label.description: add: what it means, shown in the scan instead of the word.

match.description: add: the literal word, phrase or symbol (case and Hebrew vowel marks are ignored).

on.description: amounts: true = treat money amounts as sensitive, false = keep them (the default).

path.description: search: a folder (or file) to count it in, counts only.

query.description: search: the word, phrase or field name the user thinks is sensitive.
